title: Twenty-spined Radiolaria have hexagonal symmetry, not Müller's arrangement

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Twenty-spined Radiolaria have hexagonal symmetry, not Müller's arrangement

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In twenty-spined Radiolaria the spines pass through the facets of a modified hexagonal prism, giving a true hexagonal symmetry of two polar spines, six equatorial spines and two whorls of six intermediate spines; Müller's law of five four-spined circles with no polar spine does not properly apply to any case.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. IX: On Concretions, Spicules, and Spicular Skeletons

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: The true symmetry of this figure, then, is hexagonal, with a polar axis, produced into two polar spicules; with six equatorial spicules, or rays; and with two sets of six spicular rays, interposed between the polar axis and the equatorial rays, and alternating in position with the latter.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter IX, “On Concretions, Spicules, and Spicular Skeletons”; topic “Spine arrangement in twenty-spined Radiolaria”. Scope: Acantharia and allied Radiolaria with twenty radial spines (e.g. Dorataspis, Phatnaspis)

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch09-18: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.69

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The rival arrangements make precise, mutually distinguishable predictions and analysis is straightforward once 3D data exist. Public coverage can likely test examples but not the universal rejection across all relevant taxa.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Digitize 3D spine directions in twenty-spined specimens and fit the hexagonal 2+6+6+6 arrangement against Müller's five four-spined circles using angular residuals. Taxon-level model support would directly confirm which arrangement applies.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The assertion that Müller's pattern fits no case requires broad taxonomic coverage.

Suitable intact microscopic 3D specimens may be sparse.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The two arrangements make different, quantitative predictions, so spine coordinates would discriminate them cleanly. What is public is a scatter of figures rather than a downloadable angle table, and the best-preserved illustrations are not a random sample of living Acantharia. The test is standard once images are compiled, but current open archives only partly cover the named genera.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure the latitudes and counts of the twenty spines. Hexagonal symmetry predicts two polar spines, six equatorial spines and two alternating whorls of six; Müller's arrangement predicts five four-spine circles and no polar spine. A systematic match to one angular template and not the other decides the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Acantharia, the main living twenty-spined group, are poorly represented in polycystine image databases and their skeletons are rarely preserved.

Older sources are drawings that may already embody one or the other symmetry scheme.
